description:
Democrat Scott Colom has a razor-thin lead over Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, in a state that hasn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly 40 years and no Black person to the Senate since Reconstruction. 

Tuesday is the deadline for voters to resolve any ID issues on provisional ballots and also for counties to receive absentee ballots postmarked on or before Election Day. Counties must certify their results by November 13. 

Both Colom and Hyde-Smith have assembled extensive teams ready to observe and potentially challenge ballot-counting procedures ahead of Mississippi’s December 3 deadline for certifying the results. 

CNN's Annie Grayer reports and George County, Mississippi Court Clerk, Chad Welford, explains the remaining count in his Republican-leaning district. Also, CNN's Kate Bolduan speaks with Mississippi journalist Ashton Pittman identifies ballots yet to be counted in a Democrat stronghold.

Russia’s last independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta shut down after more than 30 years, bringing an end to one of the country’s best-known outlets for investigative journalism. The newspaper says it was forced to cease operations after years of mounting pressure from Russian authorities. 

CNN's Fred Pleitgen visited the newsroom as it closed its Moscow office for the final time and spoke to co-founder Dmitry Muratov, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 for his efforts to safeguard freedom of expression.
title: Russia’s last independent newspaper goes dark

author: CNN
description:
Chuck Schumer is confident he’ll continue leading Senate Democrats after they captured the chamber’s majority in dramatic fashion on Tuesday. Not all Democrats are so sure.

During a post-election gathering Saturday in Washington, DC, two Senate Democrats — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan — declined to back Schumer for the job, and Slotkin said she would not rule out running herself. A third Senate Democrat who appeared at the conference, Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona, said he planned to support Schumer but echoed calls for Senate Democrats “to do things differently than we’ve done before.”

“There should be no coronation of the next Democratic leader,” Van Hollen said. “I’ve said very clearly that we need to have a discussion in the Democratic caucus, we need to understand what the Democrats are going to do with this new responsibility and these new powers, and nobody should get a blank check without a full understanding of the caucus as to where we’re going
title: Schumer faces skepticism over majority leader role

description:
President Donald Trump responded to last week’s GOP drubbing by initially suggesting that he might soften his approach, expressing openness to collaborating with Democrats. 

But after growing increasingly agitated by the midterm results, Trump named longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff. 

Choosing a MAGA loyalist considered one of the most powerful hardline voices in his inner circle signaled a plan to flex even greater executive authority. Miller was the architect of Trump’s aggressive deportation campaign and other controversial policies that tested the bounds of White House power — yet also spurred voter backlash, contributing to the GOP’s historic electoral losses

The separate statements come amid growing concern over Huang’s close relationship with an executive from Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed, Alice Huang. Several US outlets have reported that American officials suspect Alice Huang, no relation, has fed intelligence to China and helped smuggle advanced artificial intelligence chips into the country. 

CNN's Will Ripley has the details and technology journalist Jacob Ward says the scandal is putting Nvidia's board of directors in "an impossible position." Also, Sen Chris Coons (D-DE) comments on possible implications to American national security and CNN tech reporter Clare Duffy reports on the market reaction.

description:
US President Donald Trump has offered his clearest indication yet that intensified diplomacy could avert another major round of fighting with Iran, in the wake of his party’s disastrous midterm election results. 

Trump told CNN on Sunday that renewed US military attacks are “highly unlikely” if Tehran makes progress toward an agreement on its nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. He also told CBS’ “60 Minutes” that he was “not looking to” escalate the war. 

CNN's Jim Sciutto shares details from his conversation with Trump. Former NATO Supreme Allied Commander James Stavridis, former US Army Major Harrison Mann and former Deputy Director of National Intelligence Beth Sanner break down Trump's options to end the conflict with Iran.
